To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
in androgen responsive human prostate cancer cells androgens control gap junction formation by regulating the expression level of connexins (the gap junction proteins) post-translationally.
androgens control gap junction formation and degradation by rerouting the constitutively degraded pool of connexins to the cell surface and enhancing assembly into functional gap junctions.
in human prostate cancer cells: (a) Cx32 is regulated post-translationally, and (b) the extent of gap-junction assembly is regulated post- translationally.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how gap junctions are regulated by hormones and growth factors in normal and cancer cells.
the mechanisms of gap junction assembly and degradation.
the regulation of the formation and degradation, as well as the function of gap junctions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
androgen regulates the formation and degradation, and the assembly into gap junction, of the Cxs in human prostate cancer cells.

the androgen-induced formation of gap junction is a result of a post-translational mechanism that involves the rescue of Cx32 from degradation and that this is the first report of the androgen-regulation of the assembly of Cx32 into gap junctions.
androgen regulates Cx32 expression at multiple levels, including transcriptional, translational and post-translational levels.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
androgens regulate gap junctions by modulating Cx protein expression levels.
androgens regulate Cx32 and hence gap junctions by controlling their formation and degradation.
the formation of gap junction and its degradation are regulated by androgens in human prostate cancer cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that

in the prostate epithelium, gap junctions are regulated by androgens and that the androgen-regulated formation of gap junctional communication may have important roles in the morphogenesis of the prostate epithelism, and in the progression of prostate cancer.
androgens regulate gap junction assembly and turnover post-translationally, by controlling the degradation of Cx32, and possibly other Cxs, in the early secretory pathway.
